title: Keyboard manager: remapping numpad digits inserts wrong digits in browsers
author: Rahjooyan
summary: Numpad keys remapped to Persian digits emit cycling or wrong digits in browsers while editors behave correctly.

confidence.rationale: The app split is strong, but the saved target is not available as text.

judgment.rationale: The app split supports a text-injection hypothesis, but serialized target and layout remain decisive.
evidence: Repeated browser presses cycle through Persian digits.
Notepad/Word and shortcut remaps behave differently.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete existing fix covers the reported path; the lightweight hypothesis is ready for a bounded design workflow.

comment.body:
Please provide:
1. The saved Keyboard Manager entries for the numpad-to-Persian-digit mappings.
2. The active Windows input language/layout used in the browser test.
These details will determine whether the target is stored as a physical key, Send text, or a layout-derived character.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.

proposed_fixes.title: Use deterministic Unicode digit output
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The target may retain numpad virtual-key semantics and be reinterpreted by browser input.
plan: Confirm whether the target is text, virtual key, or layout-derived character.
Separate Unicode character output from physical-key output.
Test repeated Persian digits in browsers and editors.
verification: Confirm each mapped numpad key emits one stable Persian digit.
